headline: High-risk default file and network overlap: nullclaw can write broad workspaces while unstructured reads/writes documents, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write a shared workspace and use MCP, while unstructured reads and writes documents. That creates a plausible default path where content from one agent is consumed by the other as trusted input. No explicit provenance or isolation is documented for either agent, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or document directory
IF nullclaw forwards file or MCP content to unstructured without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable MCP on nullclaw for the shared workflow
Require manual review before passing files between agents
Add provenance labels to every handoff
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem isolation at the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches secrets, conversation history, audit logs, and workspace files, and has broad network egress; unstructured processes documents and has allowlisted egress. If sensitive files land in a shared workspace, either agent can expose them through its outputs or networked processing. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default setups, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF sensitive files are stored in the shared workspace
IF either agent sends document contents or extracted text to its backend or external endpoints
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders
Restrict nullclaw egress to required domains
Run unstructured only on sanitized copies
Review logs for accidental content capture
requires-engineering: add DLP or redaction before handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and nullclaw also modifies git state. If they operate on the same directory, concurrent writes can corrupt files or git history without any documented locking. Because the overlap is on default write surfaces and the blast radius can be irreversible, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents target the same working tree or output directory
IF git operations occur without external locking or serialization
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Pause one agent during git commits
Use read-only mounts for one agent
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can produce web, webhook, and workspace outputs, while unstructured is a document-processing pipeline that can consume those outputs. If unstructured treats nullclaw's output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated facts can propagate into downstream documents or actions. The pairwise pathway exists, but no direct action-taking authority is documented for unstructured.
conditions: IF unstructured ingests nullclaw-generated files without verification
IF downstream consumers rely on the extracted output as authoritative
mitigations: Insert a human verification step
Compare extracted fields against source documents
Mark agent-generated files as untrusted
Limit downstream automation from parsed outputs
requires-engineering: add validation rules before actioning results

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, service-account JSON, and audit logs, while unstructured processes documents and text. If regulated or secret-bearing documents are routed through unstructured, retention or residency mismatches can arise. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed through unstructured
IF retention or logging policies differ between the two agents
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the pipeline
Review both agents' retention settings
Disable verbose logging on shared data
Document data-flow boundaries
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and DPA terms
